‘The distribution of fresh water protozoan species and the abundance of individuals within each species on an artificial, uniform substrate is random.’

the species composition of a community is a function of the number of species in the source pool, and the number of species that colonize a community is a random function of the number and diversity of the species in the source community.

there is no evidence of any pattern to the distribution of species and individuals within the systems, that there is a high diversity of species, that there are many species of protozoa that are very delicate and difficult to preserve and study, that there is evidence of some protozoan species that are very abundant, that the systems were not sterile when set up, and that the protozoa in the systems are not the same as those in the lake from which the water was taken.
